title: 涙そうそう (Nada Sou Sou — Tears Falling)
description: An Okinawan-inspired ballad about grief and gratitude for a deceased older sibling. Written by 森山良子 (Moriyama Ryoko) in memory of her younger brother; composed by Okinawan band BEGIN. First recorded by Moriyama in 1998, the song became a nationwide phenomenon through 夏川りみ (Natsukawa Rimi)'s 2001 cover, which charted for over 100 consecutive weeks. The title is an Okinawan dialect expression meaning 'tears falling one after another.' The slow tempo, simple vocabulary (mostly N4 level), and deeply personal emotion make it accessible and meaningful for intermediate learners. Key vocabulary: 古い (old), アルバム (album), 励ます (to encourage), 想い出 (memory), 涙 (tears), 会いたい (want to meet).
